title: Chapter 2: The harvest fair
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: By the day of the harvest fair, three more trees had gone dark. Ines saw them at dawn and counted them twice. She went to find Oskar and found him in the market square beside Corvin Asche, a merchant from the lowland city of Peyre. Asche had come with two wagons and a ledger, and he was offering to buy orchard plots for silver. Her cousin Tomas Varga had already agreed to sell the family's lower field to him. Ines asked Oskar to close the sale until the spring could be examined. Oskar told her to go back to her rows. When Asche remarked that he had heard some trees were failing, Ines realised that nobody outside the warden house should have known. She broke her promise, climbed onto a cart and told the whole fair that four glass trees were dead and that there was salt in the wounds. The square fell into uproar. Some people rushed up the hill to look, and others pushed toward Asche's wagons to sell before the price fell. Oskar was furious. He took away her warden's key and said she was no longer a warden of Halden. Tomas shouted that she had ruined the price of their field. Only Mother Sabela stood by her. Sabela said that the old wardens had kept a map of the water under the hill, and that the map showed a gate where the spring could be reached. The map had been locked in the warden house since Oskar took office. Without her key Ines could not open the door. That night a boy named Pim, who swept the warden house for coppers, came to her window and offered to let her in.
